svg.title: Past search schematic 08: Mount Gerizim: what was dug at Tell er-Ras and on the main summit
svg.text: Past searches 08 — Mount Gerizim: what was dug at Tell er-Ras and on the main summit
Schematic plan, north up, NOT to scale. Neither campaign was a search for the scroll; entry 57's wording appears as a label only.
Two parts of the mountain (schematic)
Blue = dug (who, when); dark blue with a figure = depth reached, in metres. Ochre dashed = recorded, not dug.
Grey dashed = no excavation reported. Red = entry 57's wording, as a label: no feature here is identified with it.

TELL ER-RAS, the northern peak
R. J. Bull, with G. E. Wright
probe 1964, season 1966 (ledger S07)
1964: exploratory E–W trench
across the summit, then probes
(its line is drawn schematically)
1966: rectangular plots along
the axes of Building A, out to
the enclosure walls (Field XII)
SWP 1882: “traces of steps on
each of its four sides”; looked at
only (SWP II pp. 189–190)
Fosse: an ancient E–W cut S of
the mound; no excavation of it is
reported. Bull asked whether it is
the scroll's upper fosse and left
the question open (1968 p. 59)
N
not to scale
N slope: probes for the stairway, 1966,
found rock-cut steps in six places
Six cisterns against the N enclosure wall:
I, II, VI excavated; silt, coins AD 285–363
III–V: no excavation reported. Which side of
the wall, and the order, drawn schematically
Hadrian's temple (Building A) over an older
Building B, mostly Hellenistic pottery (Bull)
Magen: a temple of Zeus on the northern ridge,
inaugurated 160 CE (NEAEHL p. 1742)
Depths reached (Bull 1968 pp. 66, 68)
S of Building B, to bedrock: about 25 ft of
masonry ≈ 7.6 m. Inside the N wall: about
17 ft of fill ≈ 5.2 m
Entry 57 (XII 4), project translation:
“On Mount Gerizim,
under the steps of the upper pit”
The text gives the mountain, not where on it. No
step or pit on this sheet is identified with it.
↓ the main summit lies to the S; the distance is not given in the repo
W staircase
E1
MAIN SUMMIT
Y. Magen, 1983–2006 (ledger S08)
large-area excavation (blue dashed)
depths not compiled: JSP 8, JSP 20
hold the plans (not accessed)
Sacred precinct: temple first built
mid-5th c. BCE; rebuilt under
Antiochus III; destroyed c. 110 BCE;
Samaritans rebuild it, early 4th c. CE
Mansion, Area P (40 × 40 m): a
courtyard cistern in building IV;
its size, date and fill not given.
Festus coin K35264 at locus 5178;
the feature it lay in is unknown
S wing: 9 m wide staircase, 7 steps preserved
Fortified enclosure in the SW corner, near the W staircase (its size not given)
Late Roman fortress at the precinct's NE corner
Church of Mary Mother of God, 484 CE (Zeno),
rebuilt by Justinian. Its building destroyed the
Hellenistic compound to its foundations; only
the outer walls survived (p. 1746)
E staircase: up to 23 m wide, 34 m long,
c. 57 steps rising 15.5 m, from a two-chambered
lower gate to a four-chambered upper gate (p. 1747)
Area E, E slope: building E1 (“Bakers' Fort”),
staircase of 15 steps, 8 × 2 m (p. 1745)
Who did what, when
Fieldwork and visits the repo records. Dates as stated.
Neither dig was a scroll search
SWP survey, looked at only: the knoll cut off
by a ditch, steps traced on its sides; on the
summit a church in a fortress and cisterns.
Allegro (books): did not visit. He put his
item 58, “Gerizim”, at Cypros near Jericho
Bull: surface survey of Tell er-Ras.
Bull with Wright: a probe of two to three
weeks in summer; an E–W trench, then probes.
Six weeks from 31 May (Field XII of the
Shechem expedition): plots on Building A's
axes; probes for the N-slope stairway.
A further season planned from 3 June; no
report of it in the repo.
Magen: the sacred precinct, the Hellenistic
city, the mansion and three staircases; about
16,000 coins.
Depths given
S of Building B: about 25 ft (≈ 7.6 m) of masonry, down
to bedrock.
Inside the N wall: about 17 ft (≈ 5.2 m) of fill.
Bull 1968 pp. 66, 68; feet converted at 0.3048 m. Magen:
no depths compiled in the repo.
Placements proposed for entry 57
Repo atlas: Mount Gerizim, best-supported (medium); no
specific step or pit identified.
Milik (DJD III p. 274), hedged: an earlier phase of the
stairway up to Hadrian's temple. Not tested.
Bull (1968 p. 59): the fosse as the scroll's upper
fosse, asked as a question. Not dug.
What no source in the repo reports
Digging in the fosse, or beneath any step or staircase.
Work in cisterns III–V; what locus 5178 was.
Any deposit of the scroll's kind (S07, S08).
Sources
Ledger S07–S08, research/history/salvage_records: Bull & Wright, HTR 58 (1965) 234–237; Bull, BA 31
(1968) pp. 59, 66, 68. Magen, NEAEHL 5 (2008) pp. 1742–1747 (registration extract). SWP II pp.
187–190, DJD III p. 274 (tables/phase5_reports.csv). JSP 19 p. 159 (locus 5178 follow-up). Allegro
1960 pp. 75–76, 1964 pp. 71–72 (extracts). Text: translation_en.json XII 4.
How it was drawn
Schematic, after the ledger's wording; Magen's site plan (NEAEHL p. 1743) used only for rough
positions, nothing traced. Not to scale; the distance between the two parts is not in the repo.
What it shows
Bull trenched Tell er-Ras to bedrock (≈ 7.6 m) and Magen excavated the main summit, 1983–2006. Both
dug a named place for its buildings, not for the scroll. Neither reports a deposit.
What it does not show
That entry 57's place was searched. No report in the repo describes digging in the fosse or beneath
any step, and no source identifies the scroll's step or pit.
